title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Real estate portfolio management
audience: Owners of small real estate portfolio management businesses who look after several rental properties for landlords and want a management offer that justifies its fee on value.
learningOutcomes: Write a portfolio management offer with a clear outcome, time frame, the owner's tasks and a fair guarantee
Identify the friction and risk an owner carries when handing over a portfolio, and reduce them
Price a management offer on value and cost, not only on time, with its fee basis stated

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will manage your rentals' is a service. 'I will manage your three units under a written appointment: I will complete a condition inspection with photos at each change of tenant, respond to maintenance requests within a time frame you agree, send a monthly statement on a fixed date, and show you each trust transaction' is an offer. The owner is buying a portfolio that is looked after, and certainty about where the money is and what has been done to each property.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: State the outcome: the properties managed, the tasks covered and the standard of records kept. Set time frames for maintenance responses, statement dates and inspection intervals, and agree them in writing. List what the owner must do, such as approving maintenance above an agreed amount and providing keys, compliance certificates and insurance details. Add one certainty element, such as condition reports with photos and a monthly statement. Name the risk you carry, and the risk you do not carry. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, for example leasing, tenancy management, marketing, and works above a set value, because a written quote or agreement can become binding once accepted (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes, last updated 1 August 2025). Queensland requires an appointment for a letting agent in writing, and the appointment must disclose any commission (Property Occupations Act 2014, sections 102 and 105, current as at 6 June 2025; excerpt read only).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make onboarding, approvals and reporting simple for the owner. A single intake form for each property, a standard inspection checklist, a maintenance approval threshold, and a fixed statement date each remove a decision or a worry. An owner who knows what they will receive, when, and what they must approve will value the offer more. Fewer steps and fewer decisions for the owner usually support a higher fee, because the owner is paying for reliability and less personal time, not only for the work itself.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and workmanship
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services and cannot be excluded by contract, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services (business.gov.au, Warranties and refunds, last updated 27 May 2025). Do not guarantee the things you do not control, such as a tenant's payment, a vacancy period or a rent level, because a claim you cannot substantiate or afford creates a risk. In Victoria, a business is generally given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault at no charge (Consumer Victoria, Services not done with due care and skill, last updated 13 October 2023). Offer a fix-first commitment for your own work, such as re-doing an inspection report that is wrong, and state its limits.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: No source in the research for this course gives a management fee percentage, a fixed monthly fee or a fee benchmark for any state. The fee must therefore come from your own costs and hours, and any stepped package must be built from that. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin, so check the fee against cost before adding any premium (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes). A stepped package, for example leasing only, full management, and full management with maintenance coordination, lets the owner see what each step adds (Jobber Academy, Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). That is an older, general service article and not property management data. Show one clear total and whether GST is included, and confirm the fee basis in the appointment. Queensland law allows commission to be claimed only for actual amounts agreed under the appointment (Property Occupations Act 2014, section 88; excerpt read only).

procedure: Write the portfolio outcome for the owner in one sentence the owner would repeat.
Set time frames for maintenance responses, statement dates and inspection intervals, and record how often past work met them.
List what the owner must approve or provide, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a condition report with photos and a monthly statement.
Decide the fix-first and guarantee terms, and check that you can afford them.
Price the fee from your own cost and hours, state its basis in the appointment, and check it against cost and time.

workedExamples.situation: A landlord with three rental units in Queensland asks why one manager's fee is higher than another's. The manager has not yet built a fee from the business's own costs and hours.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer, state its fee basis, and decide how to answer the landlord's question.
workedExamples.reasoning: The manager writes the appointment in writing, lists the services in each package, and states the fee basis and any commission in the appointment, as the Queensland Act requires for an appointment and its commission (sections 102 and 105, excerpt read only). The manager builds the fee from cost and hours rather than copying a rival's figure, because no fee benchmark was found in the research. The fee amount is left blank in this lesson, since no source gives one. The manager can answer the landlord by showing what each package includes, the response times and the reports the landlord receives, and by stating that commission can only be the actual amounts agreed under the appointment (section 88).

commonErrors.error: Making a guarantee about rent, occupancy or tenant behaviour that you do not control
commonErrors.prevention: Limit guarantees to the work you control, such as response times and the accuracy of your reports, and cost them before you publish them.

commonErrors.error: Stating a fee or result you cannot substantiate, such as a rent increase you have not measured
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have measured or can show, and get the owner's consent before using their details.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Letting and rent collection for reward can need a licence. In Queensland, real estate agent licences and resident letting agent licences cover letting property and collecting rent for others for reward (Property Occupations Act 2014, sections 26 and 27; excerpt read only). Check the rule for each state where you operate. Victorian residential rental manager licensing was not verified for this course.
Pricing statements are covered by the Australian Consumer Law. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, Setting prices: what's allowed, last modified 15 July 2026).

qualityStandard: Every management offer is written down, with scope, exclusions, owner tasks, time frames, the fee basis and the guarantee terms.
Offer and pricing decisions are checked against cost and time, and against the licence and appointment rules in the state where the properties are.
documentationEvidence: Written management offer with scope, exclusions, time frames and fee basis
Dated cost and time check for the fee
Signed appointment or agency agreement for each property, and the decision made
summary: A management offer promises a managed portfolio, time frames, certainty and a fair guarantee.
A higher fee follows from clearer value and reporting, not from longer hours alone.
Check the state licence and appointment rules before you publish a fee, and do not guarantee outcomes you do not control.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a management offer does the owner buy?
options: Your hourly rate and your office
Your software brand and your logo
How many years you have been in the business

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a management guarantee cover?
options: Every tenant's rent payment, whatever happens
Work you control and can afford, such as response times and report accuracy
Any vacancy period, with a refund of the fee
Nothing, because owners cannot claim against a service

knowledgeChecks.question: A landlord asks what a manager's fee covers. What should the offer show?
options: A single figure with no scope, no exclusions and no fee basis
The services included, the exclusions, the fee basis and any commission in writing
A vague promise of results and a request for a deposit with no terms

officialReferences.title: Prepare quotes (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: Says a written quote becomes binding once accepted and that a quote should recover cost plus a margin. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.

officialReferences.title: Setting prices: what's allowed (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: States that misleading price statements are prohibited. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.

officialReferences.title: Property Occupations Act 2014 (Queensland)
officialReferences.covers: Excerpt only (first 100,000 characters). Says commission may be claimed only for actual amounts (section 88) and sets out appointment and commission content (sections 102, 104 and 105). Full text of sections 102 to 105 was not reviewed.

officialReferences.title: Property management (NSW Fair Trading)
officialReferences.covers: Covers short-term rental only. Says a written agency agreement is needed for commissions and costs, and that deposits are trust money. Long-term management is not covered.

Supports: a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge; no fix-window length given.

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Older general service source; supports stepped packages. No property management figures.

business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', https://www.business.gov.au/Products-and-services/Fair-trading/Warranties-and-refunds, last updated 27 May 2025. Supports: consumer guarantees for services; no-refunds lines do not override service rights.

consumer.vic.gov.au, 'Owners corporation managers: financial information', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/licensing-and-registration/owners-corporation-managers/running-your-business/financial-information, last updated 30 November 2017. Supports: owners corporation managers hold money in trust, avoid mixing and disclose costs. This applies to strata management, not residential rental management.
